methodological_rigor.justification: Small retrospective cohort (N=48; docetaxel n=25, cisplatin n=23) with non-randomized treatment allocation. Selection bias acknowledged: cisplatin vs. docetaxel chosen based on cancer type and renal function status, not randomization. Appropriate statistical tests (unpaired t-test, Wilcoxon rank-sum, χ² test, Kaplan-Meier, log-rank) but multivariable analyses 'failed to converge due to data sparsity,' authors acknowledge. No blinding of outcome assessors. Follow-up only 90 days post-PD, limiting survival data. Short median follow-up (55 vs. 46 days) constrains prognostic inferences.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study (LoE 2b) comparing HIPEC drug regimens in malignant ascites management—clinically relevant but limited by small sample, non-randomization, and short follow-up. Direct clinical application pathway identified: docetaxel preferred over cisplatin based on nephrotoxicity differential (4% vs. 30.4% renal impairment). However, ORR/DCR/KPS improvement rates non-significantly different, suggesting modest discriminatory value for selecting between agents in clinical practice.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods adequately detail HIPEC procedure, drug dosing (Endostar 60 mg, docetaxel/cisplatin 60 mg/m²), temperature control (42–43°C), and outcome definitions (CR, PR, SD, PD per WHO criteria). STROBE partially adhered: inclusion/exclusion criteria explicit, blinding not mentioned, flow diagram absent. Data availability completely absent: no repository cited, no statement on patient-level data or biospecimen access. 'Scientific Research Board waived informed consent for study participation' raises transparency concerns.

novelty_literature.justification: HIPEC for peritoneal metastases established (Spratt 1980 cited). Endostar + cisplatin combination known for pleural effusions/ascites; docetaxel's peritoneal pharmacokinetics (AUC 1000× higher than IV) also documented. Present study is comparative head-to-head of two regimens already in clinical use; no novel drug, no new mechanism, no pathway discovery. Docetaxel's lower nephrotoxicity is predictable from known metabolism differences (hepatic vs. renal excretion).

writing_presentation.justification: Logically organized with clear treatment protocol diagram (Fig. 1), results presented with response rates and safety data. Discussion mechanistically explains Endostar + HIPEC effects (VEGF inhibition, heat-mediated drug penetration, chemotherapy mechanisms). However, limitations candidly acknowledged: small sample size, lack of multivariable analysis feasibility, non-randomized design, reliance on KPS (suggested future tools: MOSS, SCL-90). Speculative discussion of mechanisms without functional data.

key_strengths: Clinically relevant comparison of two feasible HIPEC regimens in treatment-refractory malignant ascites (failed ≥2 prior chemotherapy lines)
Clear safety signal identified: cisplatin-associated nephrotoxicity (30.4% vs. 4.0% docetaxel; P=0.045) with actionable clinical implication
Comprehensive safety monitoring: kidney function, blood counts, hepatic function tracked; well-defined adverse event grading (CTCAE v4.0)
Explicit treatment protocol description enables replication of HIPEC procedure; Endostar timing justified via 'vascular normalization window' principle
key_concerns: Small, non-randomized retrospective cohort (N=48) with indication bias: cisplatin/docetaxel chosen based on cancer type and baseline renal function, not randomization—treatment allocation not comparable between groups
Multivariable analyses failed to converge due to data sparsity; univariate comparisons only—confounding by peritoneal cancer index, baseline creatinine, specific cancer type not adjusted
No significant difference in primary efficacy endpoints (ORR 64% vs. 56.5%, DCR 92% vs. 91.3%, KPS improvement 48% vs. 43.5%, P>0.05)—suggests drugs equivalent, limiting practice-changing potential
Very short follow-up (90 days post-PD for responders; median ascites control 55 vs. 46 days)—insufficient for survival outcomes or long-term safety assessment
No data availability statement; no blinding of outcome assessors; authors waived informed consent for study participation
Mechanistic speculation regarding vascular normalization window and heat-mediated drug penetration not experimentally validated
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent small retrospective comparison identifying actionable safety signal (docetaxel reduces nephrotoxicity vs. cisplatin in HIPEC) but limited by non-randomization, small sample, and equivalent efficacy. Appropriate for specialized oncology journals with minor revisions addressing confounding adjustment and longer follow-up planning.
